messages:
maria.rowe: Heads-up — spotted what looks like a service account key in Sentry breadcrumbs from the third-party ingest path. GCS requests show an internal svc-account email. Not sure how long it's been exposed.
alex_chang: link to the error? can you paste the event id or stacktrace? :eyes:
maria.rowe: https://sentry.redwood.ai/issue/RED-3456 — payload includes `Authorization: Bearer <long-json>` and a base64 blob that decodes to a JSON with `client_email` and `private_key_id`.
ops-bot: Incident-Alert: potential credential exposure detected (channel: #eng-security). Ticket created: INC-2026-312.
sanjay.patel: yikes. first cut: rotate that service-account key, revoke any existing keys, and rotate any Vault-wrapped ciphertexts that used the same key. Also lock down RBAC for the ingest topic.
kevin: Quick q — is Vault involved here? Our Vault uses GCP KMS auto-unseal, but secrets for the partner ingestion (signed URLs / SA keys) are stored in Vault kv-v2 and wrapped with transit. If the SA key itself leaked, rewrap transit ciphertexts with a new KMS key only if the KMS key was compromised.
maria.rowe: Vault KMS key has no signs of being leaked. This looks like someone pasted the SA key into a partner payload that ended up in Sentry. So root action = revoke SA key + create new key + push to partner. Also make new token short-lived.
alex_chang: agreed. recommended steps we should run now:
- revoke compromised SA key: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=ingest@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
- create new key and upload to Vault: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create key.json --iam-account=... && vault kv put secret/ingest thirdparty_key=@key.json`
- update partner config and confirm receipt
- rotate any dependent signed URLs, and invalidate cached tokens.
security-oncall: set incident severity to P2 for now. Notify Legal + Product for partner disclosure. Also we need to preserve audit logs: export GCP audit logs and Sentry events to the incident ticket before we purge anything.
sanjay.patel: who can run the revoke? I can do it but want @maria to confirm which key id to delete.
maria.rowe: key id is `f4a2-9c3d`. Please rotate and then post new key to Vault with a TTL policy. Also add an ACL in Vault so only `eng-ingest` and `sec-bot` can read that path.
kevin: small ops note — after rotation, we should flip partner integration to use workload identity (OIDC federation) instead of long-lived SA keys. That avoids future plaintext keys in payloads.
alex_chang: agree. short-term: rotate keys. medium-term: roadmap task for workload-identity migration and rotate all current integrations. I'll create a GH issue.
maria.rowe: audit queries to run (GCP):
- last 72h keys usage: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.iam.admin.v1.CreateServiceAccountKey" OR protoPayload.methodName:"SignBlob"' --project=redwood-platform --freshness=72h`
- access to ingest bucket: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="gcs_bucket" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:ingest@' --limit=50`

please run and dump to the incident ticket.
ops-bot: Ticket INC-2026-312 updated: tasks assigned (rotate-keys, dump-audit, notify-partner, legal-notify).
security-oncall: RBAC lock suggestion: temporarily remove `roles/storage.objectAdmin` from the compromised SA and add a narrow role `roles/storage.objectViewer` if write wasn't required. Let's minimize blast radius.
sanjay.patel: noted. After revoke+new key, I will run a script to find all Vault entries that reference the old key id and re-encipher them with transit: `vault write transit/rewrap/plaintext key=ingest` (will coordinate with Vault custodian).
maria.rowe: partner notification draft: "We found a credential that appears to have been accidentally included in a payload to your integration endpoint. We have rotated the credential and recommend you update to the new key immediately. We're available for a joint verification."
kevin: also ask partner to scrub logs and rotate any cached copies on their side.
alex_chang: timeline: can we rotate within 30 min? who is doing it?
maria.rowe: I will perform revoke + new key and push to Vault (T+20m). @sanjay will rewrap Vault ciphertexts (T+40m). @kevin will draft partner note and set up a Zoom if they need help (T+1h).
security-oncall: good. make sure to retain copies of the leaked payload and Sentry event for the forensics channel. do not delete until legal signs off.
ops-bot: Reminder — runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/credential-exposure. Steps are prepopulated for this incident.
kevin: done drafting partner message, posted to ticket for review.
maria.rowe: rotated and pushed new key to Vault. updated INC-2026-312 with key fingerprint `f3b8-7d2a`. Confirmed old key revoked.
sanjay.patel: starting rewrap now. will post progress logs.
kevin: emailed partner and requested log scrub + confirmation. they responded "will rotate on our side and confirm within 30m" :thumbsup:
security-oncall: nice work. postmortem checklist: note how the key ended up in payload, consider adding a lint rule in SDK to detect long-looking PEM blobs in outgoing requests, and enable Sentry data-scrubbing rule for auth headers.
maria.rowe: created follow-up tickets: TECHDEBT-558 (workload-identity migration), SECURITY-449 (Sentry scrubbing rule), and OPERATIONS-721 (Vault rewrap automation).
ops-bot: INC-2026-312 closed by maria.rowe (pending partner confirmation).
